Name: Cross-AZ Data Transfer
Cost Driver: Cross-AZ traffic with service-specific billable endpoints and exemptions
Mitigation: Prefer same-AZ client access where compatible with resilience requirements; measure each traffic leg
Order of Magnitude: USD EC2-to-ElastiCache cross-AZ example: $0.01/GiB on the EC2 side; 1000 billable GiB/day for 30 days = $300 for that side; confirm regional pricing
Gotcha: ElastiCache does not charge its side of this transfer; do not apply this example to every EC2/RDS path or sacrifice Multi-AZ availability

Name: Internet Egress
Cost Driver: Outbound internet bytes by source region and usage tier
Mitigation: Compare CDN and origin transfer costs; compress responses and reduce unnecessary downloads
Order of Magnitude: USD Ohio example rate: $0.09/GB; 1000 billable GB = $90 before taxes or negotiated discounts
Gotcha: The 100 GB monthly AWS internet-transfer allowance is shared across eligible services and regions with exclusions; billable GB means after applicable allowances

Name: NAT Gateway Processing
Cost Driver: Gateway-hours plus every GB processed and applicable transfer charges
Mitigation: Use gateway-type VPC endpoints for eligible S3/DynamoDB traffic; compare paid interface endpoints for other services
Order of Magnitude: USD us-east-2 zonal example: $0.045/hour + $0.045/GB; 730 hours and 1000 GB processed = $77.85 before transfer and public IPv4 charges
Gotcha: Gateway Load Balancer endpoints are not free S3 gateway endpoints; cross-AZ routing and regional NAT per-AZ hours can add charges

Name: DynamoDB On-Demand Pricing
Cost Driver: Consumed read/write request units including item-size and consistency effects
Mitigation: Use on-demand for variable workloads; compare measured utilization before selecting provisioned capacity
Order of Magnitude: USD us-east-1 Standard table example: $0.625/million WRUs + $0.125/million RRUs; storage and optional features excluded
Gotcha: One nontransactional write up to 1 KB uses 1 WRU; a strong read up to 4 KB uses 1 RRU; eventual reads use half and transactions double units

Name: DynamoDB Provisioned vs On-Demand
Cost Driver: Provisioned capacity-hours versus consumed request units
Mitigation: Model actual utilization and scaling headroom; include indexes and table class rather than assuming a fixed savings multiplier
Order of Magnitude: USD us-east-1 Standard provisioned example: $0.00065/WCU-hour + $0.00013/RCU-hour before eligible allowances; compare against on-demand units
Gotcha: Provisioned-to-on-demand switching is allowed up to four times per rolling 24 hours; on-demand-to-provisioned can be done at any time; idle provisioned capacity still bills

Name: S3 Request Pricing
Cost Driver: Request counts by operation and storage class plus retrieval and transfer
Mitigation: Reduce unnecessary requests; evaluate S3 Inventory for repeated listings and include Inventory or batch-operation charges
Order of Magnitude: USD regional pricing is per 1000 requests by operation/class; storage is separately per GB-month; do not reuse S3 Tables or Express prices for Standard
Gotcha: LIST uses the S3 Standard PUT request rate; small objects can add request and metadata costs; retrieval charges depend on class

Name: S3 Storage Classes
Cost Driver: Storage GB-months plus retrieval and minimum-duration/object-size charges
Mitigation: Choose a named storage class based on access frequency and recovery time; include Intelligent-Tiering monitoring fees
Order of Magnitude: Minimum storage durations: Standard-IA and One Zone-IA 30 days; Glacier Instant Retrieval and Flexible Retrieval 90 days; Deep Archive 180 days
Gotcha: Glacier is not one price or retrieval tier; One Zone classes do not survive AZ loss; small objects may not qualify for Intelligent-Tiering automation

Name: GPU Instance Costs
Cost Driver: Whole-instance runtime and attached storage/networking for training or inference
Mitigation: Benchmark cost per completed job or token; use interruptible capacity only with recovery support; right-size GPU memory and utilization
Order of Magnitude: USD instance-hour rates depend on region and exact SKU/purchase option; obtain a current quote rather than reuse the old p4d or cross-cloud per-GPU estimates
Gotcha: A multi-GPU instance quote is not a per-GPU quote; Spot availability and interruption risk matter; commitments charge even when idle

Name: CloudWatch Logs Ingestion
Cost Driver: Ingested GB plus retained compressed GB-months and query/feature usage
Mitigation: Set retention and reduce redundant logs without dropping required audit events; compare log classes and archive destinations
Order of Magnitude: USD us-east-1 vended-log example: first 10 TB delivery tier $0.50/GB and archival $0.03/GB-month compressed; before allowances or delivery credits
Gotcha: Rates depend on log source/class/destination and volume tier; ingestion GB differs from compressed storage GB; queries and custom metrics bill separately

Name: Load Balancer Idle Costs
Cost Driver: Running load-balancer hours plus capacity units and optional reservations
Mitigation: Delete unused load balancers; consolidate only when isolation and routing requirements allow
Order of Magnitude: USD us-east-1 example: ALB or NLB base $0.0225/hour; 730 hours = $16.425 before LCU/NLCU usage and public IPv4 or transfer charges
Gotcha: ALB LCU billing uses the highest usage dimension; first 10 processed rules are free in the rule-evaluation dimension; capacity reservations can bill while idle

Name: RDS Multi-AZ Costs
Cost Driver: Engine and deployment-specific compute plus storage/IOPS and backup charges
Mitigation: Select availability from recovery objectives; compare the actual Multi-AZ deployment and engine in the pricing calculator
Order of Magnitude: USD regional instance-hour and GB-month rates depend on engine and deployment; no universal 2x multiplier or free Aurora replica compute
Gotcha: Do not substitute read scaling for an HA design; Multi-AZ replication transfer is free but cross-AZ EC2 client traffic can bill on the EC2 side; extended support can add cost

Name: Kubernetes Cluster Overhead
Cost Driver: Cluster support-tier hours plus worker compute/storage/networking and optional management features
Mitigation: Upgrade Kubernetes before extended support; right-size workers and compare full EC2/Fargate/Auto Mode bills
Order of Magnitude: USD EKS base cluster fee: standard support $0.10/cluster-hour or $73 per 730 hours; extended support $0.60/cluster-hour or $438 per 730 hours; confirm regional pricing
Gotcha: Worker resources are separate; Auto Mode and Provisioned Control Plane have additional charges; system-pod overhead must be measured rather than assumed

Name: GCP BigQuery Pricing
Cost Driver: On-demand bytes processed or edition-specific slot-hours plus storage and other operations
Mitigation: Prune columns/partitions; use dry runs and maximum bytes billed; compare editions for sustained workloads
Order of Magnitude: USD us-central1 on-demand example: $6.25/TiB after the first 1 TiB/month per account; 10 billable TiB = $62.50 before storage and other operations
Gotcha: TiB means 2^40 bytes; LIMIT does not reduce bytes scanned; new capacity purchases use editions/slot-hours rather than the legacy $2000 flat-rate quote

Name: VPC Endpoint Costs
Cost Driver: Interface endpoint-hours in each AZ plus data processed
Mitigation: Use free gateway endpoints where eligible for S3/DynamoDB; compare interface endpoint totals against NAT processing
Order of Magnitude: USD interface endpoint example: $0.01/endpoint-ENI-hour + $0.01/GB at the first processing tier; one endpoint in 3 AZs for 730 hours = $21.90 before data; confirm regional pricing
Gotcha: Each service endpoint and AZ adds hourly cost; cross-region PrivateLink adds transfer charges; do not generalize gateway endpoint pricing to interface endpoints

Name: Container Registry Storage
Cost Driver: Stored image/artifact GB-months plus chargeable outbound transfer
Mitigation: Expire unused images with lifecycle policies; keep rollback artifacts and reduce image size
Order of Magnitude: USD us-east-1 private-repository example: $0.10/GB-month; 50 billable GB stored for a month = $5 before transfer and other features
Gotcha: Use measured stored bytes rather than image count times nominal size; replication adds destination storage and transfer; same-region pulls to AWS compute are free of ECR transfer charges

Name: Secrets Manager Costs
Cost Driver: Stored secret-months and API calls plus related service usage
Mitigation: Remove unused secrets safely and cache reads within rotation requirements; compare alternatives against security and operational needs
Order of Magnitude: USD published example: $0.40/secret-month + $0.05/10000 API calls; 1000 secrets held all month = $400 storage before calls and related charges; confirm regional pricing
Gotcha: New secret versions are not separately charged as secrets; rotation infrastructure and KMS usage can add charges; self-hosting is not automatically cheaper

Name: Data Transfer Between Regions
Cost Driver: Cross-region outbound bytes by source/destination pair plus replication operations
Mitigation: Model each direction and replication destination separately; retain required disaster-recovery isolation
Order of Magnitude: USD S3 us-west-2 to us-east-1 example: $0.02/GB; 1000 billable GB/month = $20; 1000 billable GB/day for 30 days = $600 before other charges
Gotcha: The same rate is not universal across services or regions; replication requests and destination storage are separate; distinguish GB/month from GB/day

Name: Lambda Invocation Costs
Cost Driver: Request units plus memory GB multiplied by billed execution seconds
Mitigation: Benchmark memory/CPU settings against duration; use provisioned concurrency for latency requirements only after pricing its additional charges
Order of Magnitude: USD us-east-1 x86 on-demand example: $0.20/million requests + $0.0000166667/GB-second at the initial duration tier before allowances
Gotcha: Eligible monthly allowance is 1 million requests and 400000 GB-seconds; provisioned concurrency has separate pricing; larger asynchronous payloads may consume multiple request units

Name: ElastiCache Node Costs
Cost Driver: Node-hours or serverless storage GB-hours plus ECPUs
Mitigation: Compare engines and measured memory/request demand; include replicas and commitment utilization
Order of Magnitude: USD us-east-1 Valkey Serverless example: $0.084/GB-hour stored + $0.0023/million ECPUs; excludes transfer and backups
Gotcha: Valkey minimum metered storage is 100 MB; Redis OSS and Memcached minimum is 1 GB; ECPUs depend on bytes and CPU rather than request count alone

Name: FinOps Tagging Strategy
Cost Driver: Unallocated direct and shared costs obscure ownership
Mitigation: Define account/project hierarchy and metadata standards; enforce supported provisioning checks and document shared-cost allocation
Order of Magnitude: Measure unallocated cost as a percentage of actual spend; no universal 30-50% baseline or guaranteed savings percentage
Gotcha: Some costs cannot be resource-tagged; AWS user-defined cost allocation tags require billing activation separately from resource tagging

Name: Managed Kafka (MSK) Costs
Cost Driver: Deployment-specific broker or cluster capacity plus storage and traffic charges
Mitigation: Compare Standard/Express/Serverless for measured throughput and retention; include replicas and transfer in estimates
Order of Magnitude: USD US East Standard-broker example: kafka.m5.large $0.21/broker-hour; 3 brokers for 730 hours = $459.90 before storage; $0.10/provisioned GB-month in the published example
Gotcha: Stored/provisioned capacity across brokers is not just logical retained data; Express and Serverless have different billing dimensions and must be priced separately

Name: CloudFront Costs
Cost Driver: Selected flat-rate plan or pay-as-you-go delivery/request usage plus applicable features
Mitigation: Compare current plan allowances and terms; improve cache hit ratio and compression; price Origin Shield separately where applicable
Order of Magnitude: USD pricing depends on plan or pay-as-you-go geography/volume; calculate using current delivery and request tiers rather than a universal Asia rate
Gotcha: Flat-rate plans and pay-as-you-go are different offers; inspect feature eligibility and plan terms before assuming invalidation or security features have the same charges
